newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy mkt expectations rise for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy mkt expectations rise for rate cut.

text.p: Italy's money market has increasing expectations for an interest rate easing within one month's time, according to a study on Friday based on implicit forward rates by the Bocconi University research arm Igier.

The implicit overnight rate in one month's time is seen at 7.41 percent, lower than the current 7.50 official discount rate and an actual market close of 8.44 percent on Thursday, the day on which Igier based its study.
Thursday's close, however, was influenced by the fact that it was the last day of the obligatory reserve period.
One week ago, the implicit overnight rate on a one-month horizon was seen at 7.68 percent while one month ago, it was forecast at 8.22 percent.

Three months out, the implicit overnight rate is seen at 7.26 percent, just down from 7.27 percent forecast a week ago. On a one-year horizon, the implicit overnight rate is seen at 6.25 percent from 6.58 percent a week ago.
In two years' time, it is forecast at 6.54 percent compared with 6.97 last week.

The spread between this projection and the implicit German overnight rate in two years, which is considered a good indicator of market confidence in Europe's economic and monetary union, shrank to 181 basis points from 213 a week ago and 257 a month ago.
The Igier study showed implicit rates staying around current levels in France and Germany but rising sharply in Britain.

The implicit British overnight rate on a one-month horizon is pegged at 5.90 percent, up from an actual market level of 5.69 percent. One week ago on the same time frame, the implicit overnight rate was seen at 4.99 percent.
